variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: ReasonML uses 'let' for immutable bindings. Mutability is achieved via explicit 'ref's, dereferenced with '^' and updated with ':='.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: ReasonML provides a JavaScript-like syntax over OCaml's powerful static type system and variant types.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Like OCaml, float and int operators are distinct (e.g., '+' vs '+.'). Reason maps structural/physical equality to `==` and `===` respectively.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Conditionals are expressions. 'switch' is used for pattern matching, bringing immense power compared to JS switch statements.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Reason has built-in imperative for loops going 'to' or 'downto' a value, useful for simple side-effect iteration.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: While loops exist for imperative tasks. They do not return values (type is 'unit').

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions use arrow syntax. The 'rec' keyword is mandatory for recursion. Labeled arguments make function calls explicit.

arrays.title: Arrays and Lists
arrays.notes: Lists are idiomatic for functional traversal. Arrays are used for fast random access and mutable state, bounded by `[|` and `|]`.

maps.title: Maps / Dicts
maps.notes: Belt is the standard library for Reason/ReScript. Belt.Map provides immutable maps with an easy API.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Reason supports exceptions but idiomatic code uses 'option' or 'result' types to model failures in the type system.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: ReasonML uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: ReasonML supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: ReasonML treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: ReasonML performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: ReasonML represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: ReasonML formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in ReasonML, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: ReasonML constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code: for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x * x
iterators.notes: ReasonML achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.code:
defmodule Person do
  defstruct [:name, :age]
  def greet(%Person{name: name}), do: "Hello #{name}"
end
oop_classes.notes: ReasonML emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in ReasonML are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: ReasonML uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: ReasonML provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
defmodule MyModule do
  import Enum, only: [map: 2]
  alias MyProject.Helper
end
modules_import.notes: ReasonML isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
